# Record an approval

You record one named person's yes on an `## Approval needed` item. You do not send anything. You do not run `apply`. You do not tick a task. You do not commit.

This is cross-cutting. It may run from any lane. It does not move work into Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

## Input

The user names the person, the source, and the quote. The source is a pull-request or thread link, or `mail`, or `meeting`, plus the date on that source. They may name the spec and the item (the first words of its line).

A missing person, source, or quote: stop and ask for that value. Do not guess. A headless run with one of them missing stops and names it.

Find the spec with `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tasks-ready-to-build>/scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs` when they did not point at a folder, as `crav1-docs/reference/running-scripts.md` says. Several matches: list them and stop.

**UI screens (1.211.0).** `$crav1-design-ui` writes one item per screen, `UI screen <name> (S<n>): ...`. When the person has more than one item, add `--item "UI screen <name> (S<n>)"` to `show` and `write`. A `Cleared:` mark on the item means a material change cleared the earlier yes; that `Approved:` line stays and no longer counts, and the new line goes below the mark.

## Show, then accept

Read [references/line.md](references/line.md). Pick the interpreter as `crav1-docs/reference/running-scripts.md` says. Run `<interpreter> -X utf8 scripts/approval_needed.py show --root <spec-folder> --person "<person>" --source-date <date> --source "<source>" --quote "<quote>" --recorder "<recorder>" --accepted <date>` and show what it prints: the `Approved:` line, the constraint, and the tasks it unblocks. An earlier quote never counts by itself. The word `yes` inside the quote is not acceptance.

The choice word is `accept`. It has to be in this run, after the line is shown. A yes from an earlier chat, or a quote that already says yes, is not `accept`.

1. **accept (Recommended).** Write the line.
2. **stop.** Write nothing.

A headless run without `accept` stops. `Missing choice. Use: accept.` It does not write.

## Write

Only after `accept` in this run. Run `<interpreter> -X utf8 scripts/approval_needed.py write --root <spec-folder> --person "<person>" --source-date <date> --source "<source>" --quote "<quote>" --recorder "<recorder>" --accepted <date> --yes`. That is the only write. It appends the `Approved:` line under that item. It does not remove the item, `Person:`, `Holds:`, `Asked:`, `Pending:`, or the constraint.

No item, or two items: stop and list them. Do not invent an item. Plan and build create items.

The personal-data and secrets check runs on the quote before the write. Follow skill `crav1-add-to-spec`, `references/sources.md`. A secret is removed and is never a choice.

## Stop

You do not edit `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `verify.md`, or `docs/system/`. You do not send, post, or reply. You do not commit, push, or open a pull request.

End with the line, who it is for, and which tasks it unblocks. the Run next reason "that approval is on record and the task can start" and the command alone in its code span `$crav1-build-tasks <T#>` When the task is a live `apply`, say the build still needs the user's own yes in that run, and the task stays unticked until then. For a UI screen item there is no task yet: the Run next reason is "that screen is signed off and the plan can cover it" and the command is `$crav1-plan-from-spec <slug>`. Leave the Uncommitted line when the spec changed.

## Run ending (1.122.0)

End as [run-ending.md](../crav1-docs/reference/run-ending.md) says.
